newsitem.title: USA: British nanny confides of death to inmate - report.
newsitem.headline: British nanny confides of death to inmate - report.

text.p: A British nanny, charged with first-degree murder in the death of an infant in her care, told an inmate she shook the baby to stop his crying but did not realise she was hurting him, the Boston Herald reported on Thursday.

The nanny, 19-year-old Louise Woodward, discussed the death with Jennifer Crawford, 20, who has a history of small-time offences, including shoplifting, receiving stolen credit cards and breaking and entering, when the two served time together in the state's prison for women, the Herald said.

"She said the baby was crying out of control, that it just wouldn't stop," Crawford told the newspaper. "She got frustrated. She picked him up by the arms and started to shake him because he wouldn't keep quiet. She said she didn't realise the damage she was doing."
Prosecutors have said the 9-month-old boy, Matthew Eappen, died in February from a blunt blow to the head.
Woodward, of Chester, England, who came to the United States a year ago to work as an au pair, has been held without bail in a Framingham, Massachusetts, prison since February.
She plead not guilty to a first-degree murder charge. If convicted, Woodward would receive a mandatory sentence of life in prison with no chance of parole.
Crawford will be interviewed by state troopers and could be one of two inmates who could end up testifying for prosecutors, the Herald said.
According to court documents, Woodward allegedly had a conversation with a second inmate, Kelly Marshall, the Herald said. The documents did not disclose what the conversation was about.
Woodward's lawyers did not return a phone call to Reuters seeking comment. They declined to discuss the matter with the Boston Herald, citing a gag order issued by the judge in the case.
